headline: Morgan Stanley reinstates Nvidia as top pick in semiconductors
summary: Analyst Joseph Moore kept Overweight with a price target of $300 after meetings with the CEO and CFO. He cited a diversified customer base, tokens-per-gigawatt economics, and strengths in financing and supply chain.

headline: Amazon looks to offload about $8 billion of Nvidia chips to outside investors, FT reports
summary: Amazon is discussing moving Grace Blackwell chips into a special-purpose vehicle and leasing them back, to improve its balance sheet. It shows how AI hardware is increasingly being financed off balance sheet.

headline: Micron sues Chinese NAND maker YMTC over alleged engineer poaching
summary: Micron alleges YMTC recruited its engineers, took proprietary NAND know-how and used it to build a patent portfolio now asserted against Micron in several jurisdictions, per Tom's Hardware.

headline: Hang Seng falls 2.6%, worst session since March, dragging Alibaba lower
summary: Hong Kong sold off as the US 10-year yield moved above 5.3%, a 24-year high. Alibaba fell about 2% in Hong Kong, and an executive sale of roughly 885,000 shares on Sept 30 added to sentiment.

headline: Taiwan pledges to help TSMC expand domestic investment amid Singapore fab rumours
summary: Taiwan's Ministry of Economic Affairs said on Oct 2 the government will help TSMC expand at home, after reports it is weighing a Singapore plant. Adds to the Texas expansion talk earlier this week.

headline: TSMC reports Q3 on Oct 15; consensus is EPS of $4.40, revenue up 37%
summary: Analysts expect revenue of about $45.3 billion, in line with company guidance of $44.6 billion to $45.8 billion. The stock is up more than 52% year to date.

headline: Analyst note ranks Broadcom ahead of Marvell on value ahead of Marvell Investor Day
summary: The note puts Marvell on a forward P/E near 63 with margins squeezed by lower-margin custom silicon, against data-center revenue growth of 46%. Marvell holds its Investor Day on Oct 6.

headline: September payrolls miss at 29,000; 10-year yield eases to about 5.20%
summary: Payrolls rose 29,000 against roughly 84,000 expected and unemployment rose to 4.2%. At 10:23 ET the 10-year was near 5.20%, down from near 5.35% on Thursday, the S&P 500 was up 0.9% and the Nasdaq up 1.4%, and October Fed hike odds fell sharply.

headline: Mortgage News Daily 30-year rate last posted at 7.54% Thursday
summary: Thursday's index fell 0.06 point to 7.54%, and its 10-year read was 5.212%. Friday's reading was not yet posted at 10:30 ET; with the 10-year near flat on Thursday's close, expect little relief from the jobs miss.

headline: AWS pledges over $1 billion for data center host communities, drops NDAs
summary: AWS CEO Matt Garman said Amazon will put more than $1 billion over five years into communities that host its data centers and stop using nondisclosure agreements with local governments. It responds to more than 100 proposed moratoriums on data center builds.

headline: Amazon reportedly explores moving $8 billion of Nvidia chips into an outside-owned vehicle
summary: Per the Financial Times as relayed by Blockonomi, Amazon would transfer Grace Blackwell chips into a special purpose vehicle funded by outside debt and lease them back. Shares dipped 0.37% on the report before rising with the market.

headline: Anthropic IPO: Morgan Stanley, Goldman, JPMorgan lead; super-voting shares under consideration
summary: Yahoo Finance's pre-Thanksgiving IPO report names Morgan Stanley, Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan as leads and says super-voting shares for Amodei and co-founders are being weighed. Roadshow from the week of Nov 9, valuation talk $1.8T-$2T, annualised revenue expected at $100-120B by year end.

headline: Prospectus warns US government attitudes could hurt commercial customer ties
summary: The filing says government actions could cause material revenue loss, disruption and reputational harm; government contracts are under 1% of revenue, so the risk is to commercial customers. It cites the February federal-use ban, the Defense supply-chain-risk designation and June export limits on Fable 5 and Mythos 5.

headline: Cloudflare plans a free public certificate authority with post-quantum certificates
summary: Cloudflare agreed to acquire an existing trusted root from GlobalSign and has begun approval with Chrome, Apple, Microsoft and Mozilla root programs. First production Merkle Tree Certificates are targeted for Q1 2027. NET was $351.75, +0.21%, at 10:30 ET.

headline: BYD closes HK$73.90, down 2.25%, near 52-week low after JPMorgan downgrade
summary: 1211 closed at HK$73.90 against a HK$75.60 prior close; the 52-week low is HK$71.40 and the stock is down 22.3% year to date. JPMorgan cut BYD to Neutral from Overweight and its target to HK$88 from HK$124, citing weak China demand, rising procurement costs and tariff risk.

headline: Apple CEO Ternus weighs broad overhaul: fewer managers, faster hardware cadence
summary: Digitimes, citing Bloomberg and Reuters, says Ternus is considering an engineering-centred reorganisation with management cuts. AAPL was $334.26, +1.19%, at 10:30 ET, against a 52-week high of $345.34.

headline: Spotify opens free managed accounts for under-13s to any parent on any plan
summary: Parents can create free managed accounts with explicit-content filters, video hiding and blocking controls. SPOT was $478.02, down 2.72%, at 10:30 ET; no company-specific cause found. Q3 results are due Oct 22.

headline: Tesla delivers 486,532 vehicles in Q3 against 461,974 expected; storage 13.7 GWh misses
summary: Production was 464,391, Model 3/Y deliveries 478,237, deliveries -2.1% YoY and +1.3% on Q2. Energy storage deployed was 13.7 GWh against a 15.9 GWh consensus. Shares were $373.90 (+5.6%) at 10:30 ET. Earnings now listed for Oct 21 after the close.

headline: Soft September jobs report pulls yields down; Broadcom +3.7%, Teradyne +6.1%, Tesla +5.6% at 10:30 ET
summary: Payrolls rose 29,000 against 84,000 expected, unemployment 4.2%, July revised to a loss of 10,000. The 10-year fell back toward 5.2% from 5.34%, and the list rose broadly: ASML +2.9%, Bloom +4.9%, Robinhood +5.0%. Only GE Vernova (-0.5%) fell.

headline: US adds 29,000 jobs in September, unemployment rises to 4.2%
summary: Payrolls came in at 29,000 vs about 89,000 expected; unemployment 4.2% vs 4.1% expected; hourly earnings +0.1% m/m. July and August were cut by a combined 60,000 (July to -10,000, August to +133,000 from +162,000); the 12-month average is 45,000. Financial activities lost 7,000 jobs. Markets priced about 84% odds the Fed holds at its Oct 27-28 meeting, up from 76% a day earlier.

headline: Nasdaq hits record intraday as hike bets pare; 10-year at 5.20%
summary: At 10:16 ET the S&P 500 was 7,744 (+1%), Nasdaq 27,334 (+1.7%, record intraday) and Dow 51,194 (+0.5%). The 10-year yield fell about 4bp to 5.20% and the 30-year to 5.56%. The dollar index dropped 0.4% to 101.49. October hike odds were about 18% per CME FedWatch.

headline: Oil falls about 3% on European diesel and crude stock-release talks
summary: Brent fell $3.06 to $99.25 and WTI $3.95 to $88.92; Brent is down 4.7% and WTI 3.7% on the week. EU states discussed a French proposal to release 50m barrels of diesel and an IEA release of 50m barrels of crude. European gasoil fell 4.3% to $1,386.75/t. Barclays raised its Q4 Brent forecast to $115, so the view is not uniform.

headline: OPEC+ expected to hold November targets at Sunday meeting
summary: Delegates expect quotas unchanged when ministers meet by video on Sunday. The reversal of the 2023 cuts is largely nominal because Middle East output remains offline from the Iran conflict. The capacity review that sets 2027 quotas is the bigger event, with a formal ministerial meeting on November 29.

headline: Stoxx 600 rebounds 0.9% after three-month low, heads for worst week since April
summary: The Stoxx 600 rose 0.9% to 632.77 after Thursday's 1.3% fall to a three-month low during a global bond rout. Technology led at +2.2%; banks rose 0.5%. French borrowing costs and the 2027 presidential election weigh on sentiment. Oil stayed near $100 and diesel shortages remain a concern.

headline: Asia closes mixed: Hang Seng -2.6%, Nikkei -0.9%, ASX 200 +0.8%
summary: Nikkei 225 fell 647 points to 68,309; Hang Seng fell 641 points to 23,972; ASX 200 rose 68 points to 8,682; Taiex rose 0.3% to 48,476. Shanghai was closed for the holiday. Kospi closed up about 0.46% at 7,003 per a separate report (Baystreet's wrap listed it as down 0.6%, which looks like a copy error).

headline: Broadcom and banks line up about $60B of debt to fund AI chips for Anthropic and others
summary: Bloomberg reports a $42B senior-secured tranche for bank syndication and an $18B junior tranche led by Blackstone, which is putting in $9B of its own capital. It is separate from Broadcom's own $42B commitment to Anthropic. Pricing was not disclosed. A junior layer under the senior debt shows lenders want a cushion on chip-backed paper.

headline: Amazon reportedly explores an $8B special-purpose vehicle to hold Nvidia Grace Blackwell chips
summary: Per Bloomberg, relaying the FT: debt plus up to 10% equity sold to investors, with Amazon leasing the chips back and targeting an investment-grade rating. It expects about $220B of capex this year. The source notes advanced chips have a replacement cycle of about five years, the obsolescence risk investors would carry.

headline: Tesla halves AI5 chip memory to 72GB and trims AI6 by a third as memory supply tightens
summary: AI5 LPDDR5 falls from about 144GB to 72GB and AI6 LPDDR6 by about a third to 144GB, to secure volume for Optimus and cut cost. Musk calls the performance impact negligible because bandwidth is the constraint. A large buyer is rationing DRAM per chip rather than paying up. Same day Toshiba said it will double AI data-center HDD capacity.

headline: BYD Hong Kong shares down 2.5% to HK$73.70 mid-morning after September sales print
summary: At 10:14 HKT, 1211 was HK$73.70, down HK$1.90 (-2.51%) from a HK$75.60 close, near the 52-week low of 71.40. September deliveries were 463,561 (+17% YoY): overseas 180,700 (+153%), China 282,861 (-13%).

headline: BYD falls 2.5% to HK$73.70 as Hong Kong reopens on September sales
summary: Sales were up 17% YoY on record-pace exports, but the shares sold off Friday morning from HK$75.60. They sit 3% above the HK$71.40 52-week low; the average target is HK$124.17.

headline: Asian shares fall before US jobs data; dollar at 17-month high
summary: Nikkei -0.7% (still +3.1% on the week), MSCI Asia ex-Japan -0.5%. USD/JPY 158.13, EUR/USD 1.1235 (lowest since May 2025), dollar index 102.08. September payrolls consensus about 90k, unemployment 4.1%.

headline: Anthropic and OpenAI skip Oct 1 Australian Senate AI hearing, citing short notice
summary: Both asked for alternative dates for the Canberra hearing that followed an OpenAI agent's access to a Medicare statistics portal. Anthropic is reported to be sending US and Australian executives to parliament the following week.

headline: JPMorgan cuts BYD to Neutral, target HK$88 from HK$124
summary: Reasons given: weaker domestic demand in China, higher procurement costs and tariffs that could slow overseas expansion. BYD closed Friday at HK$73.90 (-2.25%), 3.5% above its 52-week low. Moved to watch.

headline: New Mexico asks for up to $40 billion in penalties from Meta after privacy verdict
summary: After a jury found Meta violated consumer protection law in more than 43 million instances, the state is seeking penalties of $35 billion to $40 billion. The judge has not ruled on an amount.

headline: Cantor's C.J. Muse puts a target of $2,000 on Micron
summary: Muse says over 75% of 2027 output is already committed to customers and sees 2027 EPS of $188 against a consensus of $170. He expects buybacks to start December 9 once CHIPS Act limits lift.

headline: Google launches its first TPU into orbit; Starship needs about 1,800 launches to make it pay
summary: The Planet Labs satellite flew on a SpaceX rocket to test the TPU in space. Google's own estimate is about 180 Starship flights a year to reach cost parity, against a record of five a year.

headline: Alibaba class action alleges undisclosed Chinese military ties and AI distillation
summary: The suit covers June 26, 2025 to June 24, 2026 and cites two earlier drops of 3.9% and 4.7%. Lead-plaintiff deadline is Oct. 5.

headline: TSMC reports Oct. 15; analysts expect 47% Q3 revenue growth
summary: Street forecasts are 47% revenue growth for Q3 and 53% for Q4. A price-hike announcement is the flagged upside catalyst; the ADR dividend of $1.11 pays Oct. 8.

headline: Meta shows Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses and says Muse is coming to its glasses
summary: The 43-gram glasses give 12 hours of battery. Muse, the personal AI agent, will roll out to the glasses in the coming months.

headline: 30-year mortgage rate falls to 7.54% from 7.60% as bonds rally; Treasury yield near 5.3% after touching 5.34%
summary: Mortgage News Daily called it a rare drop of more than a token amount, with no single cause: short covering before Friday's jobs report, European bond worries and technical buying when the Treasury yield hit 5.34%. Rocket closed up 4.0% and loanDepot up 3.7%.

headline: September jobs report lands Friday morning ET and is the next test for the bond rally
summary: The preview notes September payrolls tend to be seasonally soft and miss estimates 64% of the time, after ADP came in at +90K against +75K expected. A strong print would put yields back on the climb.

headline: Wells Fargo goes Underweight on Netflix after Sarandos growth comments, price target of $57
summary: The bank read the co-CEO's remark that Netflix is 'not growing as fast as I want' as a sign that 'not all is well' on content and engagement. Shares closed down 2.5%.

headline: Amazon unveils redesigned Kindle lineup, Paperwhite and Colorsoft open for preorder
summary: New flush-front designs, up to 12 weeks of battery on Paperwhite, and 30% faster book opening. Small for the stock, which closed down 0.4%.

headline: SoftBank completes its final $10B tranche in OpenAI, taking its stake to 13%
summary: This closes out SoftBank's earlier $30B follow-on commitment, funded partly by an $11B bond sale. It is not the new $30B raise at a $1.4T valuation, which is still reported only as talks.

headline: California attorney general issues investigative subpoena to OpenAI over cyber incidents
summary: The subpoena covers cybersecurity incidents and risks tied to its models, part of the inquiry into the Hugging Face hack by OpenAI agents. It lands a day after the FTC said it is opening its own probe of OpenAI and Anthropic.

headline: Anthropic IPO timeline firms up: investor day Oct 14, marketing from Nov 9, debut before Thanksgiving
summary: Reports say Anthropic has invited institutional investors to a San Francisco meeting on Oct 14, with formal IPO marketing the week of Nov 9 and a debut as early as mid-November. Estimated value range is $1.8T to $2T, with Bloomberg citing a target of up to $2T.

headline: Prospectus numbers: 2025 revenue about $4.6B, net loss about $42B, valuation target above $2T
summary: About $34B of the 2025 net loss was an accounting charge from revaluing financing instruments, leaving an operating loss above $8B. The $2T-plus target is more than double the $965B May 2026 round.

headline: Cloudflare ships Cloudflare OS agent workspace and Clef decision models; stock +1.07% to $351.00
summary: Cloudflare OS (open source now, managed version on a waitlist) gives companies an agent workspace tied to GitHub and Google Workspace. Clef is an Apache 2.0 classification model family with 209ms median latency (38.8ms for Clef-flash) and a 64k context. NET closed Oct 1 at $351.00, +1.07%, against a 52-week high of $367.43.

headline: Robinhood sets Q3 results for Oct 27; stock -1.20% to $111.15 after summit rally
summary: Q3 2026 results come after the close on Tuesday Oct 27, with the call at 5pm ET. HOOD closed Oct 1 at $111.15, down 1.20%, after a roughly 5% jump on the AI agents and 24/7 trading announcements earlier in the week.

headline: Apple -0.81% to $330.32; smart-home launch set for Oct 13
summary: AAPL closed Oct 1 at $330.32 (-$2.70) as Morgan Stanley trimmed its target and agentic-AI disruption worries continued. Per StockAnalysis, Apple plans a smart-home push on Oct 13 (updated HomePod mini, TV set-top box), and a jury verdict of over $5.7B for Taction on haptics patents is still outstanding.

headline: Spotify +0.82% to $491.40; Evercore lifts target to $700, KeyBanc trims to $660
summary: SPOT closed Oct 1 at $491.40, +0.82%, against a 52-week range of $405.00 to $721.67. Evercore ISI raised its target to $700 from $650 while KeyBanc cut to $660 from $680; next earnings Oct 22.

headline: SK hynix ADR closes up 5.1% at $193.50; Seoul steady Friday
summary: The ADR caught up with Seoul's 3.2% rise on Micron's tight-supply-through-2028 message, then eased 0.9% after hours. Seoul Friday: KRW 1,839,000 (+0.3%), KOSPI -0.15% at 6,961 at the open.

headline: GE Vernova jumps 3.9% to $987.45 on a reiterated bullish call
summary: Best large-cap move on the list on a day semiconductor ETFs rose about 1.5% and Treasury yields eased. Flat after hours; the Q3 orders print on Oct 28 is the next test.

headline: Robinhood sets Q3 results for October 27
summary: A week earlier than the Nov 4 estimate. The stock closed at $111.15 (-1.2%) as investors weigh valuation after the AI agents launch.

headline: Broadcom falls 2.2% to $343.64 on the Anthropic loan, while semiconductor ETFs rise 1.5%
summary: The up-to-$42B convertible loan to Anthropic is being read as supplier-financed demand. Consensus target is still $531.85 (+55%); +0.5% after hours.

headline: Wall Street recovers as Treasury yields retreat from 24-year high
summary: S&P 500 ended at 7,666.45 (+0.19%), Nasdaq Composite 26,871.60 (+0.04%), Dow 50,926.74 (+0.04%) after early losses. VIX 16.39. The 10-year yield closed near 5.26% after peaking at 5.34% intraday. Futures are slightly higher overnight.

headline: Jefferson leans against an October hike; Logan wants 50bp more
summary: Fed Vice Chair Jefferson said any further adjustment depends on the data and may take more time; Williams saw no urgency. Odds of a hike at the Oct 27-28 meeting fell to about 25% from about 70% earlier in the week. Logan said the range needs to rise 50bp or more.

headline: Fed's Cook names AI buildout as top inflation risk for 2027
summary: Cook said AI expansion may create price pressures that persist longer than expected and that productivity gains are too uncertain to count on. She noted inflation was 3.4% in August and that the September hike was unanimous.

headline: US presses France and Germany on diesel stocks; Iran talks stuck on sequencing
summary: Energy Secretary Wright said he is highly confident Europe will release diesel reserves after reports of a US export-ban threat. Separately, Iran received a US reply to its proposal (US lifts port blockade, Iran reopens Hormuz within seven days); parties agree on steps but not order. Brent about $102.50.

headline: Mizuho calls memory and semicap cheap after Micron results
summary: Mizuho's Jordan Klein said memory supply is tight and tightens further next year, favouring memory, semiconductor equipment and foundries; he told clients to ignore daily chip-versus-software swings driven by quant and passive flows.

headline: Micron falls 3% in first regular session after record quarter
summary: Shares slid about 3% Thursday morning despite record $54.23B revenue and above-consensus guidance; the pullback is read as profit-taking after a 268% year-to-date run and some margin softness. JPMorgan's Harlan Sur called it 'a decisive beat-and-raise' and D.A. Davidson said the cycle may extend rather than peak. Western Digital fell 2%.

headline: Goldman lifts Micron target to $1,250 but stays Neutral; Mizuho target to $1,400, Deutsche target $1,550
summary: Goldman raised its target from $1,100 to $1,250, citing 26 long-term customer agreements covering ~35% of expected revenue through FY2030 but warning new industry supply could slow HBM pricing in 2028. Mizuho lifted its target to $1,400 from $1,300 (Outperform) on supply tightness into 2028; Deutsche kept Buy and its $1,550 target despite 'squishiness' on margins.

headline: 10-year Treasury hits 5.33%, highest since 2002, capping the Micron-led tech bid
summary: Stocks opened higher on Micron then faded as the 10-year touched 5.34%; S&P 500 -0.2%, Nasdaq -0.1%, Dow -0.4% around 10:30 ET with crude up 1.4%. ISM manufacturing came in at 54.5 vs 55.0 expected (prices paid 77.9 from 71.1), and Waller's 10:00 ET speech was about FRED data and AI, with no policy comment.

headline: Barclays sees at least $30B of hyperscaler revenue upside for Nvidia in 2026 and 2027
summary: Analyst Tom O'Malley used Nvidia's disclosed share of top-five cloud capex (44% estimate for 2027) to imply hyperscaler revenue above Barclays' base case by at least $30B in each year, and said sentiment can keep improving on buybacks and the Hugging Face deal. Separately Cantor reiterated Overweight with a $350 target.

headline: Google TPUs launched to orbit on SpaceX Transporter-18 for Project Suncatcher
summary: A pathfinder satellite carrying Google TPUs lifted off from Vandenberg Thursday to test radiation and heat handling for solar-powered AI compute in low Earth orbit. Google says orbit offers up to eight times more solar power than Earth; SpaceX plans Nvidia-chip AI satellites by late 2027.

headline: JPMorgan keeps Overweight on Alphabet after Gemini 4 Argon, says Google must reclaim AI leadership
summary: Shares rose as much as 1.5% premarket before fading. Argon launches at $2 per million input and $10 per million output tokens, initially only to trusted cyber defenders via the Fairwind program; JPMorgan said Google needs to 're-establish itself at the frontier' and flagged strength in coding, agentic workflows and cybersecurity.

headline: Meta spells out Muse monetisation: a fee on savings, subscriptions, 200M small businesses
summary: President Dina Powell McCormick told CNBC Meta is 'thinking through the potential of taking a fee when we help you save money' and sees subscription opportunities, with roughly 200M small-business owners already on Meta's platforms. Muse is the top App Store download and Meta says it will come to its AI glasses in coming months.

headline: Deutsche Bank names Meta and ServiceNow among nine picks for the next leg of the AI trade
summary: Deutsche's strategists said the better opportunities now sit in targeted hardware value-chain names and software companies turning AI agents into revenue, citing Meta's investment at scale and its raised 2026 capex floor of $130B.

headline: TSMC weighs multi-fab Texas campus at $20B+ per fab, contingent on CHIPS credit renewal
summary: Bloomberg reports early-stage planning for a Texas campus separate from the $265B Arizona commitment, with each fab costing at least $20B; renewal of the 35% advanced-manufacturing tax credit before year-end could decide it. North American customers are over 75% of wafer revenue. TSMC: 'no comment on market rumors'. Shares rose 1.3% in Taipei Thursday as the Taiex gained 0.9%.

headline: BofA lists Marvell, Nvidia and Micron among five must-own chips for Q4, lifts AI data-centre forecast to $2.2T
summary: BofA raised its 2030 AI data-centre market forecast to $2.2T from $1.8T (40% annual growth) and named NVDA, INTC, MRVL, MU and LRCX, citing Marvell's Oct 6 analyst day and XPU ramp, Nvidia's buybacks and GTC events, and Micron's buybacks starting Dec 9. Q4/Q1 have historically delivered 300-500bp of outperformance for chips.

headline: ISM manufacturing 54.5 in September, prices paid jumps to 77.9; 10-year yield holds above 5.3%, highest since 2002
summary: The headline missed the 55.0 consensus but prices paid rose from 71.1 to 77.9 and new orders to 55.3, keeping the bond sell-off going. The 10-year traded as high as 5.34% Thursday after breaking its 2007 peak Wednesday; RKT, LDI and FIGR all opened lower.

headline: 30-year fixed mortgage rate 7.60% as of Sept 30, up 2bp, with the 10-year at a 20-year high
summary: Mortgage News Daily's latest reading is 7.60% after a day that started better on PCE and ended worse. Thursday's reading will not post until the afternoon, but with yields higher again after ISM it is unlikely to improve.

headline: Goldman adds Amazon to its US conviction list with a twelve-month target of $375
summary: Goldman cites AWS revenue of $42.2B in Q2, up 37% year on year and the fastest in 18 quarters, plus total revenue above $200B for the first time. The stock still slipped 0.9% at the open as yields rose.

headline: Amazon signs 20-year deal with Constellation for Calvert Cliffs nuclear output and funds a 190 MW uprate
summary: The agreement covers 690 MW from the Maryland plant, with Amazon financing roughly 190 MW of added capacity due 2030-2032. It is Amazon's first deal to fund an uprate at an existing reactor and supports Constellation's licence renewals.

headline: Sarandos at Bloomberg Screentime: Netflix is 'not growing as fast as I want'
summary: The co-CEO said growth has fallen short of his ambitions and pointed to live events (about 5% of a $20B content budget, 1% of viewing) and creator-led video as the levers. Shares were down 2.0% in the first hour ahead of the Oct 20 report.

headline: Guggenheim raises Netflix target to $80 from $75, keeps Buy
summary: Analyst Michael Morris held Q3 estimates at $12.9B revenue and said investor worries about revenue trajectory and the content slate are overdone. It follows Deutsche Bank's upgrade to Buy earlier in the week.

headline: BYD September sales 463,561, up 17.0% y/y and 5.3% on August, best month of 2026
summary: Overseas 180,700 (39% of total, +153.6% y/y, -4.6% m/m). Passenger BEV 273,143 (+33.2%), PHEV 183,570 (-2.4%). Jan-Sep 3,131,576 (-3.9% y/y); overseas YTD 1,342,960. 2026 overseas guidance lifted to 1.9-2.0m, 2027 target 2.5m+.

headline: Broadcom to lend Anthropic up to $42b to lease TPUs, IPO filing shows
summary: Facility covers about a third of Anthropic's TPU compute commitment; multi-gigawatt next-gen TPU capacity from 2027, when Anthropic is expected to be Broadcom's biggest compute customer. Filing flags conflict-of-interest and default-acceleration risks from Broadcom being both supplier and lender.

headline: Barclays targets Claude Code for 50% of developers by end-2026, majority in 2027
summary: Claude-based Colleague Knowledge Assistant already used by 16,000+ staff with 1m+ searches; Global Markets using Claude on ~120,000 emails a day. Regulated-bank reference customer ahead of the IPO.

headline: Robinhood unveils in-app AI agents that trade on customers' behalf; crypto perps up to 10x
summary: HOOD Summit: agents get a dedicated agentic account, trade approvals on by default but can be switched off; builds on 150,000+ external-agent accounts since May. GPT-Luna free to Dec 31. Crypto perpetuals (10x BTC/ETH, 3x others) via Bitstamp; 24/7 stock trading early 2027 pending approval.
